title: Bad restrictions force a long path in the canonical tree
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables, let $\rho$ be a restriction of those variables, and let $d$ be a natural number. Write $f|_\rho$ for the restricted Boolean function, which sends an assignment $x$ to the value of $f$ on the assignment that agrees with $\rho$ on its fixed variables and with $x$ on its free variables. Suppose $\rho$ is bad for $f$ at depth $d$, meaning that the decision-tree depth of $f|_\rho$ — the least depth of any decision tree computing $f|_\rho$ — is strictly greater than $d$. Then the deepest root-to-leaf path of the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho$ has length strictly greater than $d$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ is a restriction of the n variables
ρ is bad for f at depth d: the restricted function f|_ρ has decision-tree depth > d
replaced:
